But nobody falls for the sofa trick twice!
%s invokes Article 50 and leaves the debate!
%s invokes Article 50… but the negotiations will drag on for years!
“VETO!” The opponent blocks the decision: unanimity required.
But the veto doesn't work this time!
Safeguard clause! All changes are cancelled.

Structural funds rain down on the field!
%s ends up sitting on the sofa!
%s is caught in an endless procedure!
%s wakes up! The summit is over.

This isn't the time for that!

You can't walk out of an official debate! It would be an admission of weakness.
You flee through the emergency exit!
You can't run: the session hasn't been adjourned!
%s makes its argument… The table is so long it will take a whole turn to arrive!
Last turn's argument finally reaches the other end of the table!
Hello, hello! Welcome to the wonderful… and slightly bureaucratic… world of the European Union!
My name is Robert Schuman. Perhaps you've heard of me: a story about coal, steel and the 9th of May… I'll tell you about it.
Since then, this world has been inhabited by strange creatures: EUROMONS! Directives, regulations, amendments, cookie banners… They live in piles of files and in the corridor carpets.
Some people collect them, others make them debate. Me, I study them. That's what we call… comitology!
But let's talk about you. This morning, two interns are expected at the European Parliament…
On the left, Alex, the new intern — a girl. On the right, Max, the new intern — a boy. Who are you?
Perfect! And what shall I officially call you? It has to be written in all 24 languages, so choose carefully.
{P}! Marvellous. I'll have it translated into Maltese right away.
This is Oliver, your fellow intern, straight from London. He's… very confident.
Hello! Don't worry, {P}, I'll be the best intern in the whole Union. Easy.
Your mission, for both of you, is simple: get ONE directive adopted. The directive ending the clock change. Parliament voted for it in March 2019…
… and since then, it's been sleeping in the Council. Like many things.

To succeed, you'll need the 8 badges of Europe's great cities, to convince the European Council, and the President of the Commission herself! Come on, {P}. Your internship starts now. It's unpaid, but very educational!
Did you know? Parliament moves to Strasbourg twelve times a year, trunks included.
The EU has 24 official languages. Your intern speaks one and a half.
Tip: caps attached to the bottle no longer get lost (Directive 2019/904).
Loading… like the end of the clock change: voted in 2019, still pending.
The European flag has 12 stars. It's not the number of countries: it's a symbol of perfection.
The Schuman Declaration dates from 9 May 1950. 9 May is Europe Day!
Euro coins arrived in people's pockets on 1 January 2002.
Since June 2017, no more roaming charges in Europe. Call your mum from Lisbon!
The universal USB-C charger has been mandatory since late 2024. Farewell, drawer of cables.
Erasmus was born in 1987. Since then, millions of students have learned to cook pasta.
The Schengen Agreement was signed in 1985 on a boat on the Moselle, in Luxembourg.
The European Parliament has had 720 MEPs since 2024.
Tip: the canteen heals your whole team. Coffee, on the other hand, heals nothing.
Tip: hold B to run. The Berlaymont's corridors are long.
The regulation on banana curvature (1994) exists… but it's mostly about quality.
The GDPR (2018) gave you cookie banners. Lots of cookie banners.
The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the European Union in 2012.
The Treaty of Rome (1957) created the European Economic Community.
The Maastricht Treaty (1992) created the European Union and planned the euro.
The Treaty of Lisbon (2007) contains Article 50. Only one country has used it.
The United Kingdom left the EU on 31 January 2020. Oliver still hasn't got over it.
Tip: Official Stamps capture weakened Euromons better.
Tip: a Euromon put to sleep by a Night Summit is easier to capture.
The Berlaymont was cleared of asbestos from 1991 to 2004. The site meeting was a long one.
The EU Court of Justice sits in Luxembourg, on the Kirchberg plateau.
The ECB is in Frankfurt. Its tower cost more than planned. Inflation, no doubt.
Simone Veil was the first President of the elected European Parliament, in 1979.
The Commission has 27 commissioners: one per country. Even for Austria's fisheries policy.
Tip: press X to open the menu.
The Danube flows through ten countries. Your shoes, only two.
On Europe Day, a rare Euromon appears. Try 9 May!
EU translations amount to millions of pages a year.
The European anthem is Beethoven's Ode to Joy, with no official lyrics.
Tip: Legal-type moves are super effective against Lobby.
Tip: Veto blocks an attack, but not your determination.
Brexit lasted so long that the word “Brextension” was invented.
Parliament has a liaison office in every member state.
Tip: talk to everyone. Even the pigeon on Place Lux.
Denmark has an opt-out from the euro. It keeps its krone, and its Vikings.
Loading 27 national opinions… 26 out of 27… Waiting for Hungary.
Wild Euromons will leave you alone for a while.
This isn't the time to use that.
Capture this Euromon to read its entry.
No save medium detected. On a DS (DS Pico, R4…), launch the game from the SD card. On an emulator, enable DLDI / the SD card, or use save states.
Report sent in 24 languages. Game saved (slot %d)!
Writing to the SD card failed. Try again.
Return to the title screen? Anything not saved will be lost.
Welcome to the Parlamentarium Shop! Everything is guaranteed to meet EC standards.
It seems your budget is… under the spending ceiling.
Thank you! And here's a Super Stamp as a gift, for the bulk purchase!
Thank you for your purchase! Invoice in triplicate.
That? It's not for sale, it's an item of strategic importance!
Goodbye! Don't forget: the USB-C charger is sold separately.
{P} switches on the Archives terminal. “Welcome to the document management system.”
You must keep at least one Euromon in your team!
Your team is full (6 Euromons maximum).
You postponed the reform. %s did not evolve.
The MEPs are arriving in the hemicycle! Tap each seat that lights up yellow before it goes out. 25 votes in 30 seconds!
Adopted by a large majority! Applause from all sides.
No quorum. The sitting is suspended…
Documents scroll across the desk. Tap each one to stamp it before it leaves the screen. 15 documents!
Tap the documents to stamp them
All documents are stamped! The administration is proud of you.
Some documents left unstamped. They'll have to go through the whole circuit again…
Cookie banners are invading the screen! Tap “Reject” on each one. If six banners pile up, you lose. Hold out for 25 seconds!
All cookies rejected! The GDPR is proud of you.
Overwhelmed by banners… You've accepted 437 advertising partners.
It's 3 a.m. and the 27 heads of state are falling asleep! Blow into the microphone (or tap the sleeping head) to wake them up. 27 wake-ups before dawn!
Everyone's awake! Agreement reached at 4:37 a.m. As usual.
The sun rises over a table of sleeping leaders. The summit is postponed.
Load the MEPs' trunks onto the train, in order: 1, 2, 3… up to 10. You have 30 seconds!
All the trunks are on the train! The session can begin.
The train left without the trunks. The MEPs will sit in their pyjamas.
This slot already contains a game. Overwrite it?
Your team is full: it goes to the Archives.
{P} has no Euromon fit to debate… {P} runs back to the canteen, head down.
There you go, a good coffee and you're off again! Your Euromons are in great shape.
Your Eurodex has %d Euromons caught out of %d seen.
It's a start! Small steps make great unions.
Not bad! You're moving faster than the daylight saving directive.
Impressive! Not even the Commission has that many files.
Extraordinary! You're a real institution all by yourself.
All aboard! The train is leaving… only a few minutes late.
Josep Borrell, the former High Representative, said in 2022: “Europe is a garden, the rest of the world is a jungle.” It caused… a bit of a stir.
Sixteen years as chancellor. Hundreds of summits. In 2015, I said: “Wir schaffen das” — we can do this.
But can you do it? I'm the first member of the Council. Nobody gets past without a compromise.
Wir haben es geschafft. You may pass. Mario is waiting for you… with a 400-page report.
July 2012, London. I said three words: “Whatever it takes”. The euro was saved. The markets calmed down.
In 2024, my report on competitiveness called for up to 800 billion of investment a year. Invest in this debate.
You did whatever it took. Kaja Kallas is waiting for you. She's… very direct.
High Representative for Foreign Affairs since December 2024. Former Prime Minister of Estonia.
The world is dangerous. I need to know whether you can stand up to the great powers. Show me.
Solid. You'll need it. President Costa is waiting for you. He hopes to finish before midnight.
President of the European Council since December 2024! It's 11:54 p.m. If we finish before midnight, it'll be a historic first.
But first: all the heads of state have fallen asleep around the table. Help me wake them up! Blow into the microphone… or tap the screen!
It's… 4:37 a.m. Well. As usual. Let's debate anyway.
The European Council approves your application unanimously! Well… unanimously minus one constructive abstention.
The President of the Commission is waiting for you on the 13th floor of the Berlaymont. It's the last step before the directive.
Ah, hello. I'm Charles Michel, former President of the European Council. I'm just… sitting. On the only chair.
In Ankara, in April 2021, I took the armchair. Ursula ended up on the sofa. They called it “Sofagate”. I never really got over it.
Welcome to the 13th floor. Yes, I live here: there's a little bedroom next to my office. It's handy for urgent files.
President of the Commission since 2019, re-elected in 2024. The Green Deal, the Covid crisis, the vaccines…
The text messages with Pfizer's boss? In May 2025, the EU General Court annulled our refusal to hand them over to the New York Times. Anyway. Moving on.
You want the daylight saving directive? Beat me. Team Europe — in the end, there can be only one.
Extraordinary. You're the best intern in the history of the Commission. Here it is… the directive ending the clock change.
All that's left is to get it signed. A formality! All we need is for…
The great powers are waiting! Antwerp, Warsaw, Piraeus… Take the train.
You saved Europe. And the directive is… in committee. As always. Thank you for everything, {P}.
BEEP BEEP BEEP! Three urgent messages arrive at the same time on every phone in the Berlaymont.
HELLO EUROPE! I have a small request. Very small. I'm putting tariffs on everything. And I'd like to buy Greenland. It's for sale, right?
Second message, from the East: “The gas tap is turned off. For your own good.” Signed: V. P.
Third message, very polite: “We are suspending our rare earth exports. Your phones will work… less.” Signed: X. J.
{P}, the directive will have to wait. The Great Powers want to bring Europe to heel. We have to go and see them. All three of them.
The port of Antwerp, Warsaw, and the port of Piraeus, in Athens. The stations are open to you. Team Europe is counting on you!
I'm NATO Secretary General. At The Hague summit, in June 2025, we committed to rise towards 5% of GDP for defence, by 2035.
And I called Donald “daddy”. Well. It was a figure of speech. He loved it. Go on, he's on the green.
In February 2025, at the Munich Conference, I explained to Europeans what democracy was. They were… surprised.
THIS IS THE MOST BEAUTIFUL GOLF COURSE IN THE WORLD. I just bought it. Well, I think so. The port too, maybe.
On 2 April 2025, Liberation Day! I held up a big board with tariffs for EVERYBODY. Even for islands where there are only penguins.
In July 2025, at my Turnberry golf course, Ursula and I made a deal: 15%. But I can change my mind. I often change my mind. It's a strategy.
And Greenland! It's big, it's white, it's beautiful. Denmark doesn't want to sell. VERY UNFAIR. We debate, and if I win, I buy it!
It was rigged. Totally rigged. Fine. We keep 15%. And Greenland stays Danish. For now. I'll post something in capital letters tonight.
Welcome to Warsaw. Prime Minister of Poland, former President of the European Council. Here, we know what freedom is worth.
Since February 2022, my country has been resisting the Russian invasion. Thank you, Europe, for your support. The palace is up there: be careful.
Take this REPowerEU kit: Europe has learned to do without Russian gas. You'll need it to keep warm in there.
Sit down. No… further away. There. In February 2022, I received presidents at this distance. It's more… comfortable.
Gas? I turned off the tap. Elections? In December 2024, Romania's Constitutional Court annulled a presidential election amid interference. I don't know what you're talking about.
Here, your arguments will take a whole turn to reach the other end of the table. Let's begin.
…Your REPowerEU kit works. Blackmail doesn't work any more. Leave, before I shorten the table.
These two pandas are on loan from China to a European zoo. It's called “panda diplomacy”. They eat 40 kg of bamboo a day. The pandas, not the diplomats.
Welcome. Since 2019, the European Union has described us as a partner, a competitor and a systemic rival. Me too, I'm all three.
You tax our electric cars — up to 35% since October 2024. We tax your cognac. And we keep an eye on our rare earths. It's balanced.
In this debate, my Euromon will change type every turn: partner, competitor, rival. Good luck keeping up.
Hmm. A partner worthy of respect. The rare earths will be on their way again. The pandas stay, they're very popular.
A yellow bear cub walks behind a container. A sign appears: “Content unavailable in your region.”
A message from the President: “The three Great Powers are demanding a summit. Right now. The G-Everything Summit. I'm sending you there.”
IT WAS MY IDEA TO HOLD THIS SUMMIT.
We are all partners. And rivals.
Right, shall we start? Me first. Everybody says I'm the best at starting.
We propose to begin… after careful consideration. In fifty years.
Why is Europe at the table? It was supposed to be on the folding seat.
THE FOLDING SEAT IS TREMENDOUS. I sell them.
Everyone talks at once. The interpreters give up. Only one solution remains: a debate.
Silence in the room. The three Great Powers look at each other… then they look at Europe.
Team Europe! Together, we are stronger than apart. That's pretty much the whole story of the Union, isn't it?
Concrete achievements, {P}. De facto solidarity. I said it in 1950. You did it in one internship.
And the directive ending the clock change? It was sent back… to committee.
The adventure continues! New trains now serve Rome, Maastricht and Lisbon. They say legendary Euromons sleep there… And someone is waiting for you at Brussels station.
An ancient statue, on the Capitol square. On 25 March 1957, six countries signed the Treaty of Rome here. Something is moving…
Here, on 7 February 1992, the Maastricht Treaty gave birth to the European Union. A giant euro coin starts to glow…
On 13 December 2007, the Treaty of Lisbon was signed at the Jerónimos Monastery. A translucent figure approaches…
In the distance, another Euromon flees: Constitutio. Rejected in 2005, it never lets itself be captured.
First day of your internship at the European Parliament! Professor Schuman is waiting for you in the Parliament hall.
Your computer shows 437 unread emails. They're all titled “Coordination meeting about meetings”.
Leopold Park. Warning: the piles of files are home to wild Euromons. Do not feed the Amendons.
Berlaymont — European Commission. Restricted access. 13th floor: the President's office (and bedroom).
“Europe will not be made all at once, or according to a single plan. It will be built through concrete achievements.” — Robert Schuman, 9 May 1950.
Hello! I don't do lobbying. I do “expertise sharing”. A canapé? It's salmon. Norwegian.
Excuse me, where's the Manneken Pis? They told me it was bigger… They've told me a lot of lies on this trip.
When I grow up, I'll be an interpreter! In 24 languages. Or a firefighter, it's calmer.
I've been covering the European Union for twenty years. My favourite headline: “Brussels says no”. It works every time.
You won… Apparently the daylight saving directive has been stuck in the Council since 2019. Good luck with that.
The Ardennes road? Not without a Euromon! Wild files are aggressive in budget season.
Halt! Nobody leaves Brussels without a Euromon. Go and see Professor Schuman at Parliament first.
The 13th floor? Only those who have convinced the European Council may go up. And you need the eight badges first.
The Europa building hosts the European Council. You need the eight treaty badges to be received.
The commissioner is… very busy. They say Team Lobby is blocking all her investigations. It's happening under the bar on Place Lux.
DG Competition only receives experienced interns. Come back with at least six badges.
Welcome to the European Parliament! Professor Schuman is waiting for you at the back of the hall.
The stairs on the right lead to the upper floors… They say one wing is haunted. I never go there, myself.
Ah, {P}! There you are at last! Punctual… give or take an hour. Blasted clock change.
Hi! I arrived an hour ago. I'm on London time, you see.
Right. You're going to work with Euromons. This Parliament's files are full of them.
I have three here, very young. They were born from great European ideas. Choose yours, {P}.
They come out of… cardboard folders?
In Brussels, everything that matters starts in a cardboard folder, Oliver. Even Europe.
GREENDEER, born of the Green Deal. COALBONNET, from the 1951 ECSC. Or ATOMINO, straight out of Euratom.
Excellent choice! Take good care of it. One well-treated Euromon is worth ten badly ratified treaties.
Then I'll take the one that beats yours. That's just smart negotiation.
Come on, {P}, a little debate to see who's the best intern?
What?! I lost to a continental intern?! That was… a trial run.
Ha! As expected. Don't take it badly, {P}, it's cultural.
Well done, both of you. Now, the mission: get the directive ending the clock change adopted.
Parliament voted for it in March 2019. Since then, it's been sleeping in the Council. You'll need the eight treaty badges to be taken seriously.
The first badge awaits you in Luxembourg, with Jean-Claude Juncker. Take the Ardennes road, to the east.
Luxembourg? Easy. I'll be there before you. See you, loser… er, colleague!
One moment, {P}! I'm Jean Monnet. I invented the small-steps method. Here's a big step: the EURODEX.
It records every Euromon you meet. And here's what you need to stamp them officially.
Weaken a wild Euromon, then throw an Official Stamp from the BAG. Europe is counting on you!
Courage, {P}! Each badge is a small stone. Just like Europe: concrete achievements.
Eight badges! The European Council awaits you at the Europa building. I'm so proud.
Talk to Professor Schuman first, young intern.
The professor's over there. Hurry up, I'm bored.
Route 1 — Ardennes Forest. Luxembourg: 3 hours on foot, 12 minutes by tax ruling.
The Ardennes forest stretches across three countries. The wild boars have never shown their passports.
One day, we'll get paid. One day…
Don't forget to fill in the satisfaction form. It's 12 pages long.
The CAP is a third of the European budget. And my combine harvester is a third of my loan.
Luxembourg-Kirchberg. EU Court of Justice, Court of Auditors, European Investment Bank. And lots of plain old banks.
To Schengen, the Moselle village where the 1985 agreement was signed. Follow the path south.
A little path leads down to the Moselle… and to Schengen.
Public transport is free here! I've been round the city 14 times by tram. For nothing. For free.
My husband was a European civil servant. He worked at the Court of Auditors. He even counted sheep to fall asleep.
The Court of Justice of the European Union has sat here since 1952. Our judgments bind all 27 states. Even on Monday mornings.
I translated a judgment into 24 languages. The Maltese version has a typo. Nobody has spotted it in ten years.
The Moselle road is reserved for holders of the Tax Ruling Badge. See Mr Juncker at the Golden Arena.
{P}! Still here? I've already visited three banks and opened two accounts. For the folklore.
Fine, OK, you're improving. I'm off to Frankfurt to see the ECB. They promised to explain interest rates to me.
Here in Luxembourg, discretion is a virtue. And an industry.
Tax rulings were legal, you know. It's just that nobody was supposed to read them. LuxLeaks, 2014, what a misfortune.
Ah, Schuman's little intern! Come, come. I started small too. Then I was Prime Minister for eighteen years.
I chaired the Eurogroup, then the Commission. I've seen my share of summits. And I've patted a lot of cheeks.
Once, in 2011, I said: “When it becomes serious, you have to lie.” So I won't tell you I'm going to let you win.
Wonderful! You've won the Tax Ruling Badge. This one's official, not confidential!
The Moselle road is open to you. Frankfurt awaits, and Christine Lagarde doesn't joke about rates.
Back to see me? Come here so I can pat your cheek. It's a Luxembourg tradition. Well, mine.
Here, on 14 June 1985, aboard the boat Princesse Marie-Astrid, five countries signed the Schengen Agreement abolishing border checks.
The Princesse Marie-Astrid! It was on a boat like this that borders were abolished. Ironic, on a river that is one.
They say a rare Euromon, Schengeon, roams the village's files. It never stops at customs.
Route 2 — Moselle Valley. Three countries in twenty kilometres. Remember to switch languages.
Free roaming is the Union's greatest gift. I've posted 4,000 photos of the Moselle.
According to my calculations, you'll win the next badge. But my calculations are rarely right.
Luxembourg crémant is PDO! Like my Cheeson.
European Central Bank. Mission: price stability. Inflation target: 2% over the medium term. Medium term: not specified.
The markets are nervous. They're always nervous. It's their job.
I still have my mattress full of Deutschmarks. You never know.
The Rhine road is closed to interns without the Euro Badge. Go and see Ms Lagarde at the ECB.
I was betting on your defeat. I lost my shirt. And my tie.
The shock was exogenous. Totally exogenous.
Welcome to the European Central Bank. Here, every word I say moves the markets. So I choose my words.
One day in March 2020, I said we were “not here to close spreads”. Italian markets plunged. You live and learn.
In my arena, the power of my attacks follows the current key interest rate. Ready for a little monetary policy?
Remarkable. Your strategy was… predictable, in the good sense. Here is the Euro Badge.
Strasbourg is to the south, past the Rhine vineyards. Roberta Metsola presides over Parliament. Never interrupt her.
Rates are stable today. Make the most of it, it never lasts.
The ECB explained everything to me: inflation, rates, the balance sheet… I didn't understand a thing. Come on, a debate, to relax!
Hmm. You know, back home in London, some people talk about leaving the Union. That would be ridiculous, wouldn't it? …Wouldn't it?
The Green Deal was presented in December 2019. Since then, we've been fighting over every comma.
My next article: “Commission wants to ban lost debates”. It's false, but it'll go viral.
Alsace wine and Baden wine look at each other across the Rhine. It used to be cannons. Progress!
Strasbourg, official seat of the European Parliament. 12 plenary sessions a year. 720 MEPs. Thousands of trunks.
I've done Brussels–Strasbourg twelve times a year since 2014. That makes… 132 moves. My trunks have more loyalty points than I do.
Help! The session starts in 2 minutes and the MEPs' trunks aren't loaded! Can you help me?
All the trunks are on board! Here, take this, it's the logistics department's official reward.
Missed… Oh well, we'll say the session is starting late. As usual. Try again whenever you like!
Well… I'll go and cry in a trunk again.
My 2,000 amendments… rejected en bloc. We'll have to start again in committee.
For the Lisbon Treaty, I had a whole trunk of notes. It stayed in Brussels.
Silence in the hemicycle! Madam President only accepts debates after a vote. Would you like to attempt a plenary vote?
Adopted by a majority! The President will receive you.
Rejected… There was no quorum. Try again!
Your vote has been recorded. The President is waiting for you.
The sitting is open. President of Parliament since 2022, re-elected in 2024: I'm used to enforcing speaking time.
You have thirty seconds. Ah, time's already up. Right, let's debate!
The result is clear: adopted! The Hemicycle Badge is yours.
And here's the European Interrail Pass. With it, every station is open to you. Your next badge is in Athens.
They say Yanis Varoufakis teaches there… on a motorbike. Take the train at Strasbourg station.
A debate? Not without a plenary vote. See the usher.
The next session is in a month. Don't forget your trunks!
Athens. Cradle of democracy, of philosophy… and of the referendum of 5 July 2015.
The Acropolis is 2,500 years old. It survived the Persians, the Ottomans and the Troika.
The port of Piraeus? Closed to visitors. It belongs to… partners. Very much partners.
Sorry, port access is restricted. Come back when the situation is… more diplomatic.
In 2015, I voted OXI. And afterwards… it's complicated.
Our report recommends even more austerity. Even for your Euromons.
We acknowledge a few errors in our forecasts. Between us.
Here for a badge? I came here by motorbike, in a leather jacket, no tie. Like at the Eurogroup meetings in 2015.
Finance minister for six months. I resigned after the referendum: 61% for OXI. Democracy is beautiful, and stubborn.
The Troika was waiting for me. You beat its agents. Show me if you're stronger than austerity!
NAI! Er, I mean: well done. Here's the OXI Badge, comrade.
Your next badge is in London. But hurry: over there, there's more and more talk of a certain exit door.
I'm off to give another lecture. On debt. On a motorbike.
Westminster. Here, on 23 June 2016, the United Kingdom voted by 51.9% to leave the European Union.
(He doesn't move. Not even for Brexit.)
Tomorrow's headline: cucumbers that are too straight. It's worked for twenty years.
In the 1990s, I was the Daily Telegraph's Brussels correspondent. I wrote some… imaginative things. Get Brexit done!
Welcome to the pub! A pint? I spent twenty years in the European Parliament explaining that we shouldn't be there.
On 28 June 2016, I told the MEPs: “You're not laughing now, are you?” They didn't laugh. You won't laugh either.
Right. You won. Take this Article 50 Badge. We've already used ours.
Still here? We've left, you know.
I have to go home. I'm no longer allowed to be an intern at Parliament. But before that… one last debate. For honour.
Thank you, {P}. Keep an eye on the directive for me. And on summer time. Back home, we'll never change it, of course.
Goodbye. Or rather… see you later. Who knows?
Oliver is gone. The London train will no longer appear at the ticket office. Next stop: Budapest, on the Danube.
Országház, the Hungarian Parliament, on the banks of the Danube. The largest building in Hungary. And the largest veto.
They say the opposition is gaining ground. A certain Péter Magyar is campaigning all over the country.
Hungarians voted on 12 April 2026. My party, Tisza, won a two-thirds majority. A new page is turning!
We built a fence. It's mostly used for photos.
The Prime Minister is about to step out for a coffee. It's a negotiating technique.
Looking for an agreement? Here, unanimity is required. And I never agree.
In 2024, I held the Presidency of the Council of the Union with the slogan “Make Europe Great Again”. Ring any bells?
In my arena, I can use my VETO every turn. And sometimes… I step out for a coffee. Like in December 2023, during the vote on Ukraine.
…Fine. I abstain. Take this Veto Badge. Officially, I wasn't in the room.
A few months later, on 12 April 2026, Hungarians vote. Péter Magyar's Tisza party wins with a two-thirds majority.
Orbán acknowledged his defeat: “painful, but clear”. Thank you, intern. Go back to Brussels: apparently DG Competition has a… lobby problem.
I've stepped out for a coffee. Come back later. Much later.
On Place Lux, on Thursday evenings, the whole of Brussels comes for a drink. MEPs, assistants… and lobbyists. Especially lobbyists.
The basement? Members only. Are you on the transparency register? No? Me neither. Come on in.
Move along, intern. Here, the grown-ups are talking business.
The energy transition? We support it. From 2080 onwards.
We respect the GDPR. We even have a 47-page cookie banner.
The suitcases? They're documentation suitcases. Very well documented.
In December 2022, Belgian police found bags of banknotes in several flats in Brussels. It was called “Qatargate”.
I was Vice-President of Parliament. I have always contested the accusations. As of this game, no final judgment has been handed down in this case.
Note: anyone implicated is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
Well, well. The intern. Do you know how many of us there are in Brussels? 25,000. And you are one.
Your daylight saving directive? I have clients who sell clocks. It will stay blocked. Unless…
Well played. I am officially declaring my defeat in the transparency register. And I'm off to the private sector. Oh, I'm already there.
Team Lobby scatters. DG Competition's investigations can resume!
We will appeal. Then appeal the appeal.
